item.title: Measuring the Neutrino Mass with $^{241}$Pu
item.description: arXiv:2611.29122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tritium has long been the isotope of choice for measurements of the absolute neutrino mass. Its low nuclear mass leads to substantial recoil energy, limiting measurements with both molecular tritium ($T_2$) and atomic tritium bound to a substrate. With a beta-decay endpoint energy and half-life similar to those of tritium, but a much larger nuclear mass, $^{241}$Pu may offer an interesting alternative. Its principal challenge is background from the beta decay of $^{237}$U. We discuss strategies for suppressing this background and compare the projected neutrino-mass sensitivities of $^{241}$Pu and tritium as a function of the background suppression.
item.dc:creator: Mustafa Anaam (Radboud University), Nicolo de Groot (Radboud University), Inge van Rens (Radboud University)

item.title: Bypassing the Nanoampere Limit: A Thick-Target Methodology for Ultra-Low-Energy Resonances in the $^{11}$B(p,$\alpha$)2$\alpha$ Reaction
item.description: arXiv:2611.30439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precise measurements of the low-energy cross section for the $^{11}$B(p,$\alpha$)2$\alpha$ reaction is critical for nuclear astrophysics and fusion energy research, yet such measurements are experimentally demanding due to the reaction's extremely small cross section. Conventional thin-target experiments are fundamentally limited to nanoampere beam currents, which restrict count rates to impractical levels at ultra-low proton energies. To overcome this limitation, we report a correction-free thick-target methodology capable of operating at beam currents of 20-60 microamperes, corresponding to a gain of over three orders of magnitude. Monte Carlo simulations of the full reaction kinematics are employed to determine the absolute reaction yield, eliminating the requirement for empirical normalization factors. At the well-known 148~keV (c.m.) resonance peak, our extracted resonance energy ($E_{\mathrm{r}} = 148.0$~keV) and level width ($\Gamma_{\mathrm{cm}} = 5.3$~keV) are demonstrated in good agreement with published data. A scheme via comparing the measured reaction probability with a theoretical extrapolation result is furtherly presented to probe low-energy resonances below 100~keV region. Preliminary measurements at proton energies of 75~keV and 100~keV reveal no evidence for additional low-energy resonances. This work provides a robust new methodology to measure cross section and resonance parameters for the p$^{11}$B reaction and offers a highly efficient tool for systematic resonance searches in the ultra-low-energy regime.
item.dc:creator: Xu-Yang Luo, Wen-Qing Wei, Shi-zheng Zhang, Wen Jiang, Bu-bo Ma, Zi-qian Zhao, Zhao Wang, Guo-Dong Wang, Lu-Lin Shi, Rui Cheng, Yan-Shi Zhang, Di Luo, Xiao Xiao, Guan-Chao Zhao, Bing Liu, Dieter H. H. Hoffmann, Jie-Ru Ren, Yong-Tao Zhao

item.title: Probing radial flow via the differential flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ using CMS open data
item.description: arXiv:2611.30904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a comprehensive study of the differential radial flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ and its $p_T$-integrated counterpart $v_0$ in Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$, using CMS open data for mid-peripheral centrality classes of 50--60\% and 60--70\%. The measured $v_0(p_T)$ distributions are compared with ATLAS measurements at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, revealing a clear energy dependence in the overall magnitude of radial flow fluctuations. Notably, the scaled ratio $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ exhibits an approximate universality that is largely independent of both collision energy and centrality at low $p_T$, persisting up to $p_T\sim3~\mathrm{GeV}$, suggesting that the integrated $v_0$ encodes most of the energy-dependent information. We compare the data with the \textsc{Jetscape} multi-stage hybrid model, using Gaussian process emulators trained on a principal component analysis of the model output to explore the full 17-dimensional parameter space. A global variance-based sensitivity analysis using Sobol indices shows that, for the Grad viscous correction, the nucleon fluctuation parameter $\sigma_k$ is the dominant source of variance for $v_0$, $v_0(p_T)$, and $v_0(p_T)/v_0$, followed by the free-streaming parameters $\tau_R$ and $\alpha$ and the nucleon width $w$. The sensitivity to the bulk viscosity peak $(\zeta/s)_{\max}$ is weak for $v_0$ but increases for $v_0(p_T)$ and for the scaled ratio. Emulator predictions, calibrated on $p_T$-integrated observables and on scaled spectra, describe the data reasonably well at low and intermediate $p_T$. Parameters calibrated at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$ also describe the ATLAS $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ data at $5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, supporting a near universal momentum dependence of radial flow fluctuations across collision energies.
item.dc:creator: Allan E. F. G. Ferreira, Thiago S. Domingues, Matthew Luzum, Cesar A. Bernardes

item.title: Emergence of collectivity in the $0^+_2$ band of $^{92}$Zr
item.description: arXiv:2611.30940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The $2^+_2 \rightarrow 0^+_2$ transition in $^{92}$Zr was observed for the first time in a high-statistics decay study of the 10-day isomer $^{92m}$Nb. Its $E2$ transition strength of 8.9(7) W.u. is enhanced by 40% relative to the ground state band, providing evidence for a collective structure built on the $0^+_2$ state which is analogous to the deformed shape-coexisting configuration in $^{94}$Zr.
item.dc:creator: E. J. Williams, P. E. Garrett, A. A. Avaa, A. B. Garnsworthy, G. Hackman, L. Mantle, S. Murillo Morales, J. R. Murias, C. E. Svensson, R. Umashankar, Y. Zhu

item.title: A high-speed and high-resolution 3D velocity map imaging system with a neuromorphic camera
item.description: arXiv:2611.28768v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An improved camera-based 3D-velocity map imaging (VMI) system was demonstrated with a neuromorphic camera. We show a machine vision event-driven camera can achieve an unprecedented latency of 2 microseconds when detecting single ion/electron with a microchannel plate imaging detector, which boosts the speed of the momentum imaging system to more than 100 kHz, while the system with a conventional frame camera is limited to a few kHz. The high spatial resolution of the camera offers additional performance boost while maintaining excellent multi-hit capability and a high time resolution.
item.dc:creator: Sulaiman Abubakar, Blessed Oguh, Akaninyene Udoikono, Hackim Musah, Suk Kyoung Lee, Wen Li

item.title: Revealing Nuclear Shape through Identified-Hadron Flow Decorrelations
item.description: arXiv:2611.30429v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Relativistic nuclear collisions encode nuclear shape in collective flow, yet the potential of identified hadrons to disentangle deformation modes remains largely unexplored. Using event-by-event viscous hydrodynamics coupled to hadronic transport, we investigate momentum-dependent elliptic-flow decorrelations of pions, kaons, and protons in central $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U collisions at 193 GeV and $^{20}$Ne+$^{20}$Ne collisions at 5.36 TeV. The identified species exhibit distinct momentum- and deformation-dependent responses, with nuclear-shape information persisting in their relative correlations even when individual deformation effects are weak. We introduce crossing coordinates $(P_{\rm cross},R_{\rm cross})$, defined by the intersection of pion-kaon and pion-proton flow-factorization ratios. Variations of quadrupole deformation and triaxiality generate distinct trajectories in the crossing plane, offering complementary constraints on both nuclear-shape parameters. The corresponding behavior persists in higher-moment correlations, while an energy comparison in Ne+Ne reveals the influence of collision dynamics. Our findings establish identified-particle flow decorrelations as a complementary approach to probing and constraining intrinsic nuclear geometry.
item.dc:creator: Hadi Mehrabpour, Abhisek Saha, Li Yan

item.title: A general formalism for electromagnetic production of two mesons on the nucleon
item.description: arXiv:2611.30755v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a general formalism for the electromagnetic production of two mesons on the nucleon, $\gamma_{\rm v}N\to\Phi_1\Phi_2B$, that can be used in single-channel as well as coupled-channel analyses over a wide range of energies. In the spirit of the decomposition introduced by Berends et al. for single-meson electroproduction, the hadronic current is expanded in a set of 16 gauge- and Lorentz-invariant matrices, four of which vanish for real photons. The corresponding Lorentz-invariant (Dirac) amplitudes can be obtained from any reaction model and are mapped onto 16 CGLN-like Pauli amplitudes, from which the five-fold differential cross section and its transverse, longitudinal, and interference response functions follow directly. Although these matrices are not all linearly independent, they follow directly from the covariant decomposition of the current, so the amplitudes can be read off from the Feynman diagrams and the observables take a simpler, more symmetric form. As a first application, we calculate the $\gamma p\to\pi^0\pi^0p$ and $\gamma p\to\pi^+\pi^0n$ reactions near threshold from tree-level nucleon Born terms. This example shows explicitly how the Dirac amplitudes are read off from Feynman diagrams and how gauge invariance, which is violated by the individual diagrams, is restored in the total amplitude and preserved when hadronic form factors are included. The formalism thus provides a versatile basis for future theoretical and phenomenological studies of double-meson photo- and electroproduction. A more complete abstract is provided in the paper.
item.dc:creator: Reddy Malik Priandika, Samson Clymton, Terry Mart

item.title: Diffractive Photoproduction of High $p_T$ Photons in Ultraperipheral Collisions at the LHC
item.description: arXiv:2611.30966v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate diffractive photoproduction of large-transverse-momentum photons in ultraperipheral collisions at the LHC, considering different collision systems and alternative descriptions of the BFKL Pomeron. We estimate cross sections and differential distributions including NLO corrections to the BFKL characteristic function and assess the prospects for measuring this process in ultraperipheral pp, pPb, and PbPb collisions. We find that the cross sections are sizable, and that future measurements in this channel can help constrain BFKL dynamics and improve our understanding of high-energy QCD.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao V. Bulh\~oes, Victor P. Goncalves

item.title: Emulator-enabled calibration and uncertainty quantification of $\beta$-decay calculations within the energy density functional theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.31141v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Predictions of $\beta$-decay half-lives of neutron-rich nuclei and their uncertainties critically impact our understanding of the astrophysical rapid neutron capture process. To provide quantified predictions within nuclear energy density functional theory, as customarily done, we perform Bayesian calibrations of two coupling constants: the isoscalar proton-neutron pairing strength and the isovector spin-density coupling. We apply an E-optimal experimental design for choosing the calibration sets. We employ the proton-neutron finite-amplitude method with Skyrme energy density functionals using emulators of half-lives and Gamow--Teller resonance energies. The calculated $Q_\beta$ values are fine-tuned to experimental values. The contributions to the half-life uncertainty from the theory error, $Q_\beta$ values, and the parameter uncertainty are all accounted for in the Bayesian framework. Our predictions for the even-even $N=126$ isotones provide the shortest half-lives for neutron-rich nuclei among the existing theoretical models, which would affect the flow of heavy-element nucleosynthesis. The proposed framework allows quantified theoretical uncertainties to be propagated to astrophysical observables such as abundance patterns and electromagnetic emission.
item.dc:creator: Yukiya Saito, Ante Ravli\'c, Witold Nazarewicz

item.title: Observation of hidden nuclear reactions on fast neutron-irradiated Lu isotopes
item.description: arXiv:2509.00539v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Some nuclear reaction channels may not be easily identified, but they can still contribute to very important characteristics like nuclear reaction cross-sections, isomeric yields, etc. The dineutron, as a bound nucleus of two neutrons, can play hidden roles, as it is considered a product resulting from fast neutron-induced nuclear reactions involving the isotopes of lutetium. When being formed in the output channels, a bound dineutron allows for an explanation for unexpected enhancement of reaction cross-sections. We used available data and instrumental spectra to deeply consider the role of the dineutron in order to understand the consequences of its formation and subsequent decay upon transformations of nuclear reaction products. As a result, we obtained experimental confirmation that the half-life of 176gLu is significantly diminished within a certain time interval, which reveals an extremely high estimation for its cross-section of 10E+11 b. This is actually due to 176gLu "burnup", followed by the fusion between 175Lu and a deuteron. This introduces the existence of novel, low-energy reactions and fusion pathways under neutron irradiation, which in-turn, leads to implications for both basic nuclear physics and high-energy physics, along with their applications.
item.dc:creator: Ihor Kadenko, Barna Bir\'o, Andr\'as Fenyvesi, Vladyslav Morozyuk, Kateryna Okopna, Nadiia Sakhno

item.title: Polarized Nuclear DVCS at the EIC
item.description: arXiv:2606.11491v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will enable a series of measurements at unprecedented energies and luminosities, providing new opportunities to investigate the microscopic structure of nucleons and nuclei at small $x_B$. Exclusive processes such as Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering (DVCS) offer unique access to the three-dimensional structure of hadrons through Generalized Parton Distributions (GPDs), while polarized electron and ion beams further enable detailed studies of spin-dependent structure. A model for coherent DVCS on polarized $^3$Heis developed and applied to simulations of for $9\times166$-GeV $e^3$He collisions at the EIC. Using this framework, the statistical precision achievable is estimated for measurements of beam-spin asymmetries and for the extraction of the Compton Form Factors (CFFs) $\mathcal H_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ and $\tilde{\mathcal H}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$. Early EIC data are found to enable precise differential measurements of the unpolarized CFF $\mathcal H_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ and to provide significant constraints on its real and imaginary components. By contrast, meaningful constraints on the polarized CFF $\tilde{\mathcal H}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ require substantially larger integrated luminosities. The kinematics of the recoil $^3$He nucleus are also examined, and the advanced far-forward detector capabilities at the EIC required to tag the intact nucleus and perform fully exclusive measurements of coherent nuclear DVCS are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Jackson R. Pybus, Xuan Li, Liliet Calero-Diaz

item.title: Constraining the Low-$p_T$ $\eta/\pi^0$ Ratio for Direct-Photon Analyses with Blast-Wave Fits to $\pi$, $K$, and $p$ Spectra
item.description: arXiv:2606.12619v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We predict the $\eta/\pi^0$ ratio at low $p_T$ ($p_T \lesssim 3~\mathrm{GeV}/c$) using the measured charged $K/\pi$ ratio and model input from a blast-wave framework with feeddown contributions. This approach can provide improved, data-constrained background estimates for direct-photon and dilepton measurements in heavy-ion collisions. In this approach, the explicit modeling of radial flow and hadronic feeddown enables an uncertainty estimate for the low-$p_T$ extrapolation of the $\eta/\pi^0$ ratio. Using central Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.76$ TeV as an example, we find that the $\eta$-related decay-photon uncertainty at $p_T \approx 1~\mathrm{GeV}/c$ is of order 10\% of the expected direct-photon signal.
item.dc:creator: Klaus Reygers, Andreas Kirchner, Aleksas Mazeliauskas

item.title: Hyper-Nuclei $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$ Production in $\sqrt{s_{\rm{NN}}}$ = 3 GeV Au+Au collisions at RHIC
item.description: arXiv:2606.22457v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The STAR experiment reports the first measurement of the $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$ hyper-nuclei yield as a function of rapidity and transverse momentum in 0-50% central Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm{NN}}} =$ 3 GeV. The $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$ is reconstructed through its three-body decay channel, $^4_{\Lambda}\rm{He} \rightarrow {}^{3}\rm{He} + \rm{p} + \pi^-$, with a statistical significance of about 9.5 standard deviations. We find that the yield of $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$ as a function of rapidity is consistent with that of $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{H}$, and the rapidity-dependent yield ratio of $^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{He}$/$^4_{\Lambda}\hbox{H}$ is consistent with that of $^3$He/t. All the measurements, as well as the transverse-momentum spectra, can be reasonably described by the JAM with a coalescence afterburner, suggesting a coalescence-based formation scenario for hyper-nuclei at this energy. The canonical thermal model reproduces the observed yield ratios but overpredicts the absolute hyper-nuclei yields.

item.title: Transverse single-spin asymmetry of forward $\eta$ mesons in $p^{\uparrow}+ p$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 200$ GeV
item.description: arXiv:2509.13497v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Utilizing the 2012 transversely polarized proton data from the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider at Brookhaven National Laboratory, the forward $\eta$-meson transverse single-spin asymmetry ($A_N$) was measured for $p^{\uparrow}+p$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=200$ GeV as a function of Feynman-x ($x_F$) for $0.2<|x_F|<0.8$ and transverse momentum ($p_T$) for $1.0<p_T<5.0$ GeV/$c$. Large asymmetries at positive $x_F$ are observed ($\left<A_N\right>=0.086 \pm 0.019$), agreeing well with previous measurements of $\pi^{0}$ and $\eta$ $A_N$, but with reach to higher $x_F$ and $p_T$. The contribution of initial-state spin-momentum correlations to the asymmetry, as calculated in the collinear twist-3 framework, appears insufficient to describe the data and suggests a significant impact on the asymmetry from fragmentation.

item.title: Toward Neutrino and Dark Matter Detection with Ancient Minerals: TEM Study of Heavy-Ion Tracks in Olivine
item.description: arXiv:2604.09732v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Solar, supernova, and atmospheric neutrinos, and possibly weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter, have been interacting in the Earth beneath our feet for billions of years. The ''paleo-detector'' technique seeks to detect and characterize the induced crystalline defects from these events, in particular from energetic nuclear recoils, which in some minerals can be preserved on these timescales. Such defects can manifest as nuclear recoil tracks, on the order of a few nanometers wide and extending up to hundreds of microns in length, which can be detected with nanoscale-resolution microscopy. In order to test the feasibility of the paleo-detector technique and to study the formation and morphology of track defects in promising mineral candidates like olivine, we use ion irradiation to artificially implant tracks to effectively mimic astrophysical particle interactions. We present a study of heavy-ion track width as a function of depth, which we relate to ion energy, in an olivine crystal irradiated with 15 MeV Au$^{+5}$ using scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Unlike previous studies, which measure tracks at the surface of the irradiated sample, we instead take measurements at various target depths via focused ion-beam sectioning of the irradiated sample. No etching techniques are used to enhance the tracks. In addition, we provide a comparison to predictions from simulations using SRIM software and previous results with a variety of ion species and energies. Notably, we find that a significant change in track continuity across the energy range studied (0.4-12.9 MeV) is indicative of the transition between electronic and nuclear stopping power dominance, consistent with the simulations' predictions. Overall, the tracks produced in olivine indicate that this mineral is an attractive candidate for paleo-detection, with robust track creation at the MeV scale.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Calabrese-Day, Emilie LaVoie-Ingram, Kathryn Ream, Hannah Ross, Joshua Spitz, Patrick Stengel, Kai Sun, Alexander Takla

item.title: Forward hadron production in pp collisions at LHC energies from an event generator based on the color glass condensate framework
item.description: arXiv:2605.15494v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate inclusive forward single-hadron production in high-energy proton--proton collisions using a CGC-inspired Monte Carlo event generator, MC-CGC. We carried out a systematic study of the sensitivity of the running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov (rcBK) evolution equation to its initial conditions by comparing three parameterizations: the McLerran-Venugopalan (MV) model and its two HERA DIS-constrained variants, MV$^\gamma$ and MV$^e$. Our results indicate that the current LHCb data favor the MV$^\gamma$ and MV$^e$ models, while the differences from the original MV model become more pronounced at higher transverse momentum and at mid-rapidity. As a complementary analysis, we also compared the dilute-dense (DHJ factorization) and dense-dense ($k_T$ factorization) frameworks. We found that the $k_T$ factorization framework provides a better description of the particle production spectra at mid-rapidity than the DHJ framework, where both the projectile and target are in the dense regime at LHC energies. Predictions for the FoCal measurements at ALICE, including the production of identified neutral mesons and jets, are also presented.
item.dc:creator: Hirotsugu Fujii, Tetsufumi Hirano, Kazunori Itakura, Yasushi Nara, Shujun Zhao

item.title: Microscopic mechanism underlying charge-radius trends in Fayans pairing
item.description: arXiv:2606.21491v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Fayans energy density functional (EDF), and in particular its pairing sector, has been claimed to be able to reproduce the experimental data of charge radii in many instances. A particularly intriguing case is that of the $ \mathrm{Ca} $ isotopes between $ A = 40 $ and $ 48 $, where charge radii exhibit a "bell shape." In our work, we examine the microscopic origin of this behavior. The pairing part of the Fayans EDF contains three essential parameters: the overall strength $ f $ and the density-dependent and density-gradient terms, $ \tilde{h}_0 $ and $ \tilde{h}_{\mathrm{D}} $. We select a number of parametrizations, fixing the overall strength $ f $ to reproduce the pairing gap of $ {}^{44} \mathrm{Ca} $. We find that some parameter sets enhance the charge radii in open-shell nuclei and reproduce the bell shape of the charge radii of $ \mathrm{Ca} $ isotopes. It is found that this effect originates from the repulsive nature of the rearrangement potential, and cannot be mocked up by a refit of the pairing strength. On the other hand, none of the parametrizations that we have considered can reproduce satisfactorily the experimental charge radii of $ \mathrm{Ca} $, $ \mathrm{Sn} $, and $ \mathrm{Pb} $ isotopes at the same time.
item.dc:creator: Tomoya Naito, Gianluca Col\`o, Xavier Roca-Maza, Hiroyuki Sagawa, Enrico Vigezzi

item.title: Perspective on Proton Transversity Distribution Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.23577v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using available information on proton tensor charges and constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD), Ansaetze are introduced for hadron-scale in-proton valence-quark transversity distributions functions (DFs). The concept of a QCD effective charge, which defines an evolution scheme for collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions that is all-orders exact, is then used to deliver predictions for the $x$-dependence of these DFs at the scale $\zeta_{2} = 2\,$GeV. Although the approach is largely algebraic, its predictions remain viable after comparisons with results obtained using computationally intensive methods. Thus, given the scarcity of data that can today be used for inference of proton transversity DFs, it may be worth using the results herein to inform and constrain related experiments and phenomenological fits.
item.dc:creator: Ke-Xin Zeng, Peng Cheng, Yang Yu, Daniele Binosi, Craig D. Roberts
